cjr.quadtree.spec.model.build_tree.description: build_tree constructs a quadtree from a natural-number depth, a rectangle, and a list of integer-coordinate points. An empty list gives Empty; a singleton gives a Leaf; and at depth zero, any nonempty list gives a Leaf containing only its first point. Otherwise, it creates four branches by filtering the full list for each child rectangle and recursively processing those points with depth reduced by one. This decreasing depth bounds recursion. No conditions on the rectangle or points are stated, and the missing definitions of midx, midy, and in_rect leave the precise subdivision and boundary behavior uncertain.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_box.description: child_box takes a natural number d, a rectangle b with integer coordinates, and a quadrant, and constructs the corresponding lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, or upper-right rectangle using b’s outer bounds and split coordinates xmin b + width d and ymin b + width d.
